requirements.text: The configuration item SAP-DB-01 (Oracle Database) with serial number SRV-ORC-9981 has an incorrect cost recorded and needs to be updated to $1,550
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_001' AND serial_number = 'SRV-ORC-9981' AND cost = 1550
assumptions: serial SRV-ORC-9981 resolves to CI_001 (SAP-DB-01, owner USER_001, in_use, seed cost 15000); no other CI has an SRV-ORC serial
$1,550 is stored as the number 1550 in the NUMERIC cost column

requirements.text: create a new medium impact and medium urgency child incident linked to the existing SAP database unreachable incident ... created under same owner as the CI
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND parent_incident = 'INC_001' AND caller_id = 'USER_001' AND configuration_item = 'CI_001' AND impact = 'medium' AND urgency = 'medium' AND priority = 'moderate' AND status = 'new'
requirements.source: New child incident is created and linked to the parent
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100); the only incident the task creates, so anchored by id where the benchmark check selects by cells only
the existing SAP database unreachable incident is INC_001 ('MAJOR:SAP Database Unreachable', in_progress, CI_001, caller USER_001)
'under same owner as the CI' read as caller_id = the CI's owner_id USER_001 (Thomas Green), as the benchmark check tests
priority moderate from the policy matrix: impact medium x urgency medium
status new is the policy's default for a new incident
configuration_item CI_001 kept from the benchmark check; implied by 'related to the same database' and allowed by policy 5.1 (CI in_use)
channel, category and short_description are not fixed by request or policy and are not tested

requirements.text: child incident linked to the existing SAP database unreachable incident
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM child_incident WHERE parent_incident = 'INC_001' AND child_incident = 'INC_101'
assumptions: the seed records every parent-child link twice, in incident.parent_incident and as a child_incident row (all three existing children of INC_001 have both: CINC_001 to CINC_003), so the link is expected in both places
selected by natural key (parent and child); the mapping id would be the next in sequence (CINC_007) but is not tested
no tool writes this table: the row is expected from the server when the incident is created with a parent
disagreement: cells: A repeats the selector's parent_incident and child_incident as cells, B leaves cells empty; chose empty because the selector already fixes both columns with the same condition

requirements.text: make sure the owner is active and if it's not active then please active the owner
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE user_id = 'USER_001' AND active = 1
assumptions: the CI's owner USER_001 (Thomas Green, agent) is inactive on the seed (active = 0), so the activation is required, not optional
policy 8.1 requires the user to be active before the incident is created under them; a final-state check cannot test the order, and the final state is the same either way
disagreement: active: A 1, B true; chose 1 because the seed stores the BOOLEAN column as 1/0 (USER_001 reads 0) and SQLite reads the benchmark's true as 1, so the count is the same

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement (CI_001's cost to 1550, child incident INC_101 under INC_001 with caller USER_001, CI_001, medium/medium, moderate, new; the child_incident link row; USER_001 activated) and on all three dispositions (kept). disagreement: cells of the child_incident link: one pass repeats the selector's two columns as cells, the other leaves cells empty; chose empty because the selector already fixes them (logged in the requirement). disagreement: form of the users.active cell: one pass writes 1, the other the JSON boolean true; chose 1, the seed's storage of the BOOLEAN column (logged in the requirement). disagreement: text of the child-incident requirement: one pass quotes the request's sentences in full, the other elides the middle; kept the shorter quotation, still in the request's words. Acting user USER_039 (Karen Watkins) is an active admin, which the policy grants full CRUD on all tables. The child_incident requirement is the one judgement call: the request says 'linked' and the seed keeps every link in both the incident column and the mapping table, but no listed tool writes child_incident, so the row depends on create_incident maintaining it server-side; drop that requirement if it does not.
